claims.claim: The game lacks support for Commander mode.

citations.review_text: No commander mode, unplayable. The only format anyone actually cares about anymore.
I hope that one day they will allow us to play commander.

It's missing the only game mode I play or find fun anymore; commander. If it had that, I might come back and play. Without commander, I'll stick to physical games with my friends or at the card shop when I have the time. It's a shame, because I'd sometimes like to play more MTG but can't get friends together or leave to the card shop to find a group. This would be a great way to get more games in, but unfortunately there is only standard 60 card gameplay.

As a lover of magic the gathering I am frankly disappointed by this. Not having commander is already pretty bad, although I can understand it for a game originally designed for mobile, however gatekeeping cards is disgusting. Cards I could literally print myself being unavailable is stupid, and disrespectful to my time. I want to enjoy this game, and enjoy it enough to want to buy cards in real life. This game doesn't not encourage me to interact with the game to buy product, it makes me want to make the product myself so I dont have to pay for printed cardboard.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the digital card economy and card pricing structure require significant financial investment to remain competitive.

citations.review_text:
Where to start...

I'm a fan of MTG. My first tournament game was in 2013. Didn't know much and had my rear handed to me several Fridays in a row. I loved the artwork and the friends I've met along the way. I used to even play the 2013 games when they came out. During those times, I hope that one day we could purchase real cards and maybe find a way to submit them to a digital card game to play with friends as well (high dreams I know).

My inital thoughts with this MTG Arena was decent. I dind't like the fact they wouldn't let you speak to other players or connect with them, but I was pleasantly surprise with the amount of decks and boosters they gave out so that you could stay updated. 

Then came the first draft tournament (the first and last one I paid for with tokens I earned). To say I had my a** reamed is an understatement. I've been bet in real life, but never this bad. 

This is where the complaints start flowing. The prices are okay, but it's a digital game. It will never be the same as buying a booster pack and having it in your hands. I'll never spend 100 dollars to be competitive at a digital card game. 

I guess if you need that Magic itch scratched, it's okay to play non-competitively. Other than that, you'll be playing against the same type of deck builder that must sped 2-300 on the perfect deck. 

If you want real enjoyment, go to a Friday Night Magic on a sealed draft tournament. At least then, you'll have a fighting chance and take home some cards you might not otherwise have.

It's a good way to learn the mechanics of the game and play if you're new/antisocial but going to your LGS and asking questions and meeting people is far less anxiety inducing than this. You should never ever spend money on virtual cards, and you will constantly have to play against the whales that do. Lots of people say MtGA is rigged and I tend to believe them. You will draw garbage and your opponent has The Most Annoying Deck Ever that he paid money for. Have fun.
This should be illegal. I've been stuck with the same deck because monetization is borderline criminal.
I love MTG, but the card economy in Arena is horrible.  Also, "Universes Beyond" is destroying Magic.

I can firmly not recommend this game without discussing the obvious problems with the balance of the game i.e. not scaling cards well, overpowering new releases by essentially copying older cards' effects and making them cheaper or stronger, thus incentivizing spending money on the newer sets

Instead, the reason I won't recommend this game is because WotC is biblically greedy: If I want to buy a prebuilt deck from the new set, even one that is discounted, I have to spend $100. That's one problem, but another problem is if I labor away to get the mythic and rare wild cards in order to get the cards I want for a deck I'm building that way, if those cards end up getting banned later down the line, I don't get my mythic or rare wild cards back, I am just completely SOL. WotC is a soul-sucking, disgustingly greedy company and I wish they would employ people that had a beating heart and cared about the product instead of soulless corporate worms whose only goal is to maximize profits to the detriment of the consumer

citations.review_text: I like MTG, but unlike your normal game with friends you are punished for trying to do some starter missions. Matched against people with well build decks and stuff. Now I'm not going to spend more money on digital cards when I already pay so much money for real cards. MTG isn't for everyone anymore. It's on the same level as playing Warhammer or something else... That's sad...

I have been an on-again off-again collector and player of Magic the Gathering dating back to 1995. I WANT to love this game, but I have found it incredibly frustrating when it comes to being a new player and match-making. 

In parts of the early game I was playing matches that were clearly against bots. Then that randomly stopped and I was playing other actual players which I am ok with, but very frustrating slogging on being unable to win a match until I get a random victory due to the opponent retiring.  Spending hours sitting there getting my teeth kicked in by people with fully custom decks built out of cards I have no access to (outside of a PAYWALL) is not a great way to entice new users to join the game. If you ARE new, prepare for a potentially VERY long slog to be able to compete in the game.

Additionally, I find it interesting that MtG doesn't do ANY type of promotion between it physical product and the digital one. I have opened several boxes and many many packs doing drafts, and I have yet to see anything for the digital game, nor any kind of special redemption opportunities in packs or boosters boxes.

citations.review_text: just dont play ranked and this game is great. unless youre okay playing top level players as a bronze since theres no rank balancing.

Yeah, nah. The real bottom line - beyond cash grab nonsense - really is just 'Hey, we have no elo system because we want to mimic a tournament :]' and thus New Player 123 gets paired against John Whale who has spent 4 trillion dollars on making the most ball-crushing deck he can muster and has been playing magic since he was 4 nanoseconds old. It's infuriating when learning and trying to earn new things really isn't an option just because of what you're paired against so frequently, turning the grind into an endless uphill battle you'll never win. Yes it's a skill issue, but it's a skill issue you can't solve by learning because it gives you no chance to learn or earn new things without ponying up the money.

I came to Arena after previous MTG games broke and don't run on modern PC's. I figured any virtual Magic is better than no virtual Magic. I was wrong. This game is clearly a predatory grab for as much money as possible and after trying it out for a couple of weeks I am walking away. 

The flat out terrible aspects of this game that make me recommend never touching it are:

- Yes, it is free to play, but as you would expect playing the game that way is an extremely tedious grind. The punishments they apply to f2p players are:
         - You will have to sit there for dozens of hours grinding with sub-par starter decks against whales who have dropped ungodly amounts of cash to have the perfect decks. Can you win? Yes, if you're lucky. But expect a fairly low win rate unless you pony up to join the arms race.
         - Want to play in the fun events or game modes besides standard? Be ready to also pay. At the time of writing this they are running special events to align with the release of their Hobbit set. Anyone can play the intro decks, which are limited to a single color and who have only around 50% of their cards actually from the new set, but if you want to play in the more unique and interesting events prepare to pay a minimum of $10 in "gems'. Or something like 6000 gold, which can represent several days of grinding f2p rewards. Oh, and that entry fee only lets you have one go at the game mode. If you lose 3 times you're out and have to pay again.

- In my experience, the match-ups just were not fun. Even in my starter deck games I was getting put against people with highly customized decks. My basic cards gave me almost no responses to play against a large portion of theirs, but they had ALL the counters against my best cards. When I finally got out of that and had a few more cards to play with I saw some improvement, but again it just felt like the match-ups were designed to make me constantly play against someone who had a deck specifically built to counter…

As a new magic player, it is an incredibly frustrating experience. the matchmaking system seems to put you up against experienced players immediately right after the tutorial games. Things happen so fast it's impossible to tell what happened and why, making it incredibly difficult to actually learn the game.

The most predatory and scamiest monetization system in human history...
New player gate keep, you wont progress anywhere unless you pay big $$$.

Matchmaking system is horrible, you will be matched with veterans in early ranks, gl winning vs broken $$$ decks.

Dont waste your money playing this sht unless you trying to waste time at work, go touch grass or play better game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the card draw and shuffler feel rigged or non-random, leading to heavily predetermined-seeming losses.

citations.review_text: this game is an absolute scam. it is RIGGED and blatantly obvious about it. but they dont care to fix it because it makes people spend more money to try and do better... when its not your cards that hold you back. its the game stacking your deck to ensure you just barely dont win. competitive modes have been a 100% loss rate using a deck that wins 90% of its games in non competition. in competition the opponents will NEVER quit. and they NEVER make a mistake... seems more like its not putting us against actual players but putting each player against an unbeatable ai that simulates being a real player. i demand absolute proof that the game is not rigged. until then i will continue to believe and share that it is.
The way this game is structured just dont ever try to draft, it costs an insane amount, and then the game is really good at making sure your draws are terrible 2/3 games

Between the relentless flood of Universes Beyond content, absurd pricing for digital packs and cards, frustrating matchmaking, and a shuffler that often feels anything but random, Arena has turned what should be an enjoyable digital version of MTG into an exhausting and overpriced experience.

Universes Beyond:
The biggest problem with magic right now is the seemingly endless flood of Universes Beyond content. Magic used to have a distinctive identity and a coherent multiverse of its own. Now, it increasingly feels like a billboard for whatever recognizable intellectual property can be licensed next. 

Pricing:
Packs are ridiculously expensive for a digital product, especially when you consider that digital cards have no resale value and cannot be traded. The cost of acquiring a competitive collection is absurd, while the game simultaneously encourages players to spend more and more just to keep up with an ever-expanding card pool.

Matchmaking:
Games routinely feel like they're engineered to produce an artificial 50% win rate rather than match players according to meaningful skill and deck quality. You can go on a winning streak and suddenly find yourself facing an endless parade of decks seemingly designed to counter exactly what you're playing. Whether this is intentional or simply the result of the matchmaking system, the experience is incredibly frustrating. When victories and losses start feeling predetermined by matchmaking rather than gameplay decisions, it undermines the entire competitive experience.

Shuffler:
The shuffler is another source of frustration. Yes, randomness will inevitably produce bad draws, mana floods, and mana screws. But Arena's draws frequently feel so consistently unnatural that it becomes difficult to trust the system. You see bizarrely repetitive opening hands, stretches of drawing nothing but lands or nothing but spells, and suspiciously convenient sequences from opponents. Even if the underlying algorithm is technically random, th…
Very unfair handsmoothing algorythm, matchmaking literally screws you up if you manage to achieve a streak of victories. If you wanna play magic, play it on paper. or play MOL (Magic Online)

The game blatantly cheats.
It's been proven.
The game deliberately forces you to lose at least 50% of the time.

Anyone can play the intro decks, which are limited to a single color and who have only around 50% of their cards actually from the new set, but if you want to play in the more unique and interesting events prepare to pay a minimum of $10 in "gems'. Or something like 6000 gold, which can represent several days of grinding f2p rewards. Oh, and that entry fee only lets you have one go at the game mode. The most predatory and scamiest monetization system in human history...
New player gate keep, you wont progress anywhere unless you pay big $$$.

Matchmaking system is horrible, you will be matched with veterans in early ranks, gl winning vs broken $$$ decks.

Dont waste your money playing this sht unless you trying to waste time at work, go touch grass or play better game.

Wayyy too P2W. Events are locked behind paywall. You have to win to profit off of events. You need practice to learn to win events. You need to play event to practice the event. And you have to pay to play the event.

Very bad game loop.

The game itself has high potential, IF they can solve the excessive p2w issue. Basically you need to pay to do anything of worth. Which would be okay if not for the fact that the pricing is not regional. So for some, you have to spend an entire month's paycheck for a measly 10 packs.

Worst part is, you cannot even grind out stuff. because any resource earning in game is time locked.

Extremely hypocritical that their slogan is "Magic for all", when in practice it is more "Magic for the rich". Amongst the most discriminatory games out there. No inclusivity for the people that don't live in the first world countries.

[b] WARNING! compared to other digital TCGs, the F2P aspects of this game are extremely predatory. [/b]

If you want to build a standard deck from scratch, and don't want to grind for it, you're likely forking over $400-$800 USD. Not an exaggeration! The three free packs they give you per set are not nearly enough to supplement any brewing, and playing the non-draft game modes don't grant you enough (or sometimes any) points to build any deck in a reasonable amount of time.

If you want to play magic online, just play a Tabletop Simulator mod instead.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience application crashes, update failures, and audio cutting out during token generation.

citations.review_text: buggy, cant update, keeps disconnecting, tried a million different 'solutions'

It'd be a wonderful game without the hysterical amount of technical issues it faces. The application crashes or fails during updates, and even occasionally on launch; which hadn't been fixed by resetting my connection, forcing a clean install, or deleting steam or MTG:A caches. It's much less of an issue but still a bother, the audio cuts out often and if you're playing a token generation deck that's even halfway decent you can plan on freezing the game or encountering more errors. Again, I'd like to clarify it's an awesome game whether you're looking for multiplayer fun, collecting, battling or really bringing out your creative side with deck-building. Unfortunately though, the developers are either under-qualified for the upkeep of the game or they're under paid to do so. Can't say I recommend taking it seriously until the dev team figures out their failures, 6/10.

I love Magic: The Gathering. It is probably my favorite game of all time. Arena doesn't do it for me. With over 1,000  hours in this game over the last  5 or so years i can honestly say that playing this was the worst experience playing magic. I have pulled my decks from edhrec now because of the FIRE card design philosophy of these new sets. Whales can dump enough money to get what they need and just stomp people even if you were running strategies that fit within your desired bracket level.
